title: The Minimal Agent Workbench
service: Workbench: the three-file minimal workbench (AGENTS.md router, agent_state.json, task_board.json) with the lesson's one-step builder turn and its definition of done, a JSON Lines board whose untouched lines keep their exact text, a picker for priorities, dependencies and the 24-hour stale-state gate, a JSON Patch line per turn for a watcher, and epics read from parent pointers

parts.lesson_anchor: AGENTS.md definition of done (the acceptance command has exited 0); agent_state.json is the system of record, read every turn; task_board.json is the queue the agent pulls from when state is empty; code/main.py load_state (AgentState(**raw)) and run_one_turn; quiz Q9 (done without running verification), Q11 (TypeError on last_run), Q14 (a crash between the two writes); outputs/skill-minimal-workbench.md (tasks without acceptance become rubber stamps); AGENTS.md is a router, not a manual (deeper docs loaded only when relevant); original AGENTS_MD rule 3 load on demand
planted_bugs: load_state is the lesson's AgentState(**raw), so the last_run and lease keys a newer workbench wrote raise TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'last_run'; the docstring keeps unknown keys in extra for save_state to write back

with no active task the pick takes only todo tasks, so the builder task a dead session left in_progress is never taken back; the turn starts T-007 as well and the ValueError 'the builder has 2 tasks in progress: T-007, T-006' surfaces two calls away, in take_turn -> save_board -> check_board
the definition of done is all(exits.values()), which reads exit code 0 as false: a task whose commands all pass goes down the blocked branch and state.blockers[0] raises IndexError
after the exit-code fix, all() of no commands is True, so a task without acceptance commands is marked done; the docstring blocks it with '<id> has no acceptance command'
load_context eagerly enumerates and reads every workspace Markdown document to build a catalog, then selects this turn's explicitly requested context; unrelated files are read on every turn
parts.timing_assert: 20 ordinary context requests in a finite workspace with600 unrelated Markdown documents under0.03s; check_board on8000 normal finished tasks under0.06s remains a supplied-validator health guard
parts.overfix_guard: dropping unknown keys clears the TypeError but loses last_run (checked first); making last_run a known field, as quiz Q11's answer does, still raises on lease; a len(set(ids)) check that cannot name the repeated id, or a dict that lets a repeat overwrite, fails the merged-board check; taking back any in_progress task picks the reviewer's R-003; deleting the one-task-in-progress check still starts T-007 instead of taking back T-006; failures judged by code > 0 or code == 1 pass the login tests that a signal killed (exit -9); correct context_paths and read_document supplied; root first, stable normalized request order, no duplicate documents, fresh selected text on the next turn, unrequested non-UTF8 Markdown never read. check_board is correct from starter; its original assertions and wrong fixes guard the provided implementation.

timing_measured.workload: 20 turn context loads, 600 unrelated Markdown files, root plus two requested docs

deviations: Part1 stacks unknown state keys, crash-left in_progress recovery and two definition-of-done mistakes (exit code0 truthiness and an empty acceptance list). The recovery error surfaces two calls away in check_board; the validator itself is supplied correct.

The load_context service extension implements the source's tiny root router and load-on-demand deeper documentation. It returns AGENTS.md plus explicitly requested Markdown paths, normalized/stable-deduplicated by a correct helper, with fresh selected text each turn. Eager whole-workspace catalog reads are newly planted, not a claim the source main.py already has that loader. The workload uses600 ordinary unrelated docs and20 real file-reading context requests; no sleep, artificial helper delay, cross-turn cache or task-priority algorithm. The supplied linear check_board retains its8000 normal-task health assertion and duplicate-id guards.

The Part1 state/turn guards preserve unknown fields, name duplicate task ids through the correct supplied check_board, and reject taking another owner's in_progress task. Context path security and complete text I/O are supplied correctly; candidate work is selecting only requested documents while keeping later turns fresh.

Task gains checks (the exit code of each acceptance command from its last run) so the definition of done leaves evidence on the board, and the lesson's prose acceptance for T-002 ('docs/api.md mentions /signup constraints') becomes the command 'grep -q /signup docs/api.md' so every acceptance entry can run.
Part 2 avoids the U+2028, ensure_ascii and sort_keys traps, which this chapter already uses more than twice; its traps are about keeping untouched lines byte-for-byte and finding the right line.

Part 3 leaves 'take back your own in_progress task' to Part 1 so it is not tested twice. The operator confirmation is the last_run value the operator looked at, which is how a confirmation counts for one run only: the run writes a new last_run. Part 3 takes last_run as an argument because this version keeps it in AgentState.extra.
Part 4 diffs against the last document it sent, so edits made between turns reach the watcher; the '/' and '~' keys come from acceptance commands used as keys of checks.

Part 5 uses parent pointers in extra rather than nested subtasks, so the board stays one task per line. An epic is a task with children, so the plan's empty epic cannot occur; loops of parents take its place, next to a parent that is not on the board.
